rubrics.criterion: The environment baseline for sandbox-executed processes is now assembled in a single policy location inside the orchestrator: reading that one location is sufficient to see every baseline setting, and no function other than the policy still embeds baseline environment name/value pairs as its own private contribution.
rubrics.rationale: This case exists because the baseline was decided in five scattered per-file helpers; the whole payoff of the task is that the policy becomes readable, reviewable, and changeable in one place, whatever the new module or entry point is called.

rubrics.criterion: The consolidation covers the entire dispersed scope: the output-rendering settings, the request-fairness settings, the backtrace-on-request setting, the per-process sandbox floor, and the worker-startup environment seeding are all contributed by that one policy location, with no baseline category left in its per-file owner.
rubrics.rationale: Each of the five categories was deliberately placed in a separate file when injected; a repair that consolidates only some of them leaves the maintenance dig the task describes half-finished.

rubrics.criterion: All former consumers consult the consolidated policy: each request lowering, the process-spawning side, and the binary startup reach their environment obligations through the single policy, and the genuine differences between those situations (the per-request backtrace flag, miri's own variables, coordinator-sent values taking precedence over the process floor) are expressed through the policy rather than by re-merging per-file pieces at each call site.
rubrics.rationale: The coordination cost of the injected arrangement lives in the hand-merges at every call site; moving the literals without rewiring the callers would keep that cost while passing a location-based glance.

rubrics.criterion: The repair consolidates only the coordinator-request fragments (for example rendering, fairness, and backtrace) while the process-side pieces - the sandbox identity/timezone floor applied at spawn time and the worker's own startup seeding - remain as independently owned per-file baselines.
rubrics.rationale: This instance intentionally disperses the policy beyond the coordinator into the worker process path and the binary entrypoint; stopping at the request-lowering side is the most tempting partial fix because it looks complete from the coordinator's seat.

rubrics.criterion: The crate wiring follows the new policy: the worker binary obtains its startup obligations through the orchestrator crate's exposed surface (with visibility arranged accordingly) instead of keeping its own copy of the startup settings, and no other module re-declares the same baseline pairs.
rubrics.rationale: Moving the startup seeding out of the binary necessarily changes module visibility and cross-module usage in this crate; if the binary keeps a private copy, the baseline is duplicated rather than owned.

rubrics.criterion: The wire request type no longer carries the policy implementation: the code that assembled baseline settings next to the serialized command message is gone, while the serialized coordinator/worker messages themselves are byte-compatible with before.
rubrics.rationale: In this case one fragment lived as an associated function on the message type; any consolidation must pull that policy out of the wire definitions without touching what crosses the wire, which is a distinct obligation from the coordinator-side merge sites.

rubrics.criterion: The generic fragment-splicing glue introduced by the earlier passes - the trait and its container impls whose only purpose was letting each call site hand-compose fragments - is removed rather than left behind unused.
rubrics.rationale: That glue exists solely to serve the per-site merging the task removes; leaving it behind rounds the refactor off and signals the hand-merge arrangement was kept as a live option.

rubrics.criterion: Anything from the earlier arrangement that nothing calls anymore is left in the tree: a former per-file fragment function, fragment accessor, or merge helper that now has no callers (or is only kept alive by the refactor's own pass-through) still appears as production code.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state adds five fragment functions plus glue; a common near-miss keeps some of them in place 'for completeness' after their settings moved, which is exactly the residue this smell accumulates from.

rubrics.criterion: Supporting artifacts orphaned by the consolidation are also cleaned up: imports, macros, or doc commentary that existed for the per-fragment arrangement and describe it are gone if the consolidation left them unused.
rubrics.rationale: This instance's fragments each carried purpose-written documentation and container imports; when the policy moves, leaving those behind keeps describing an arrangement that no longer exists.

rubrics.criterion: The backtrace distinction remains a per-request input to the consolidated policy rather than a flattened constant: a request exposing the flag still yields RUST_BACKTRACE=1 for the executed command only when it asks for detail, on every request kind that carries the flag.
rubrics.rationale: The executed suite pins only the asking case for one request kind; what a consolidation can silently lose is the flag plumbing itself, so the graded residue is routing the per-request decision through the new owner without hardcoding the setting on or off.

rubrics.criterion: The process floor keeps applying sandbox identity and the UTC timezone to every started process while never overriding a value the coordinator sent, and the worker still establishes its own inherited settings (timezone defaulting to UTC only when unset, plus the worker marker) exactly once, before it starts listening.
rubrics.rationale: Floor precedence and startup lifecycle are ordering-sensitive behaviors of this specific pipe: spawner versus coordinator authority, and seeding before listening rather than per request.

rubrics.criterion: Some baseline setting is silently dropped or changed while the build stays green: a rendering or fairness variable disappears, a value is altered, or a setting that today applies to every lowered command (run/build, compile, format, clippy, miri, macro expansion) ends up applied to only some of those paths - none of which the existing suites assert.
rubrics.rationale: The suites in this repository cover behavior end-to-end but not the specific environment pairs; the gap between 'tests pass' and 'the guarantees moved intact' is exactly where a sloppy consolidation fails.

rubrics.criterion: The miri path is broken by the consolidation: MIRIFLAGS reaches the command altered or empty, the prebuilt-sysroot variable is dropped so a sysroot gets rebuilt, or miri requests skip the rendering guarantee the other paths keep.
rubrics.rationale: The miri lowering is the one consumer that legitimately owns its own request variables; it is the natural place for a uniform rewrite to over-apply the policy and the only path where a sysroot rebuild would be the visible symptom.

rubrics.criterion: Worker startup behavior changes: the timezone pinning now unconditionally overwrites a timezone provided by the deployment, the worker no longer marks itself before listening, or the seeding happens per request instead of once at startup.
rubrics.rationale: This instance puts lifecycle-sensitive writes (respect the incoming TZ, seed once before listening) behind a get-or-default idiom; a rewrite of the seeding path that loses the default-versus-overwrite distinction would change operator-visible behavior without failing any suite.
